# Sirach Chapter 18 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_018_page_001.jpg

---

**18:1** He who lives forever created the whole universe;

**18:2** the LORD alone is righteous.

**18:3** He holds sway over the world with the span of his hand, and all things obey his will; for he is king of all things by his power, separating among them the holy from the profane.

**18:4** To no one has he granted the power to proclaim his works; and who can trace his mighty deeds?

**18:5** Who can measure the greatness of his majesty? And who can stretch out their hand to recount his mercies?

**18:6** Nothing can be diminished or added, and it is not possible to fathom the wonders of the LORD.

**18:7** When a person has finished, they are still at the beginning; and when they stop, they will be at a loss.

**18:8** What is a human being, and what purpose does he serve? What is his good, and what is his evil?

**18:9** The span of a person's years is at most a hundred.

**18:10** Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand — so are these few years in the reckoning of eternity.

**18:11** Therefore the LORD is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them.

**18:12** He sees and recognizes that their end is evil; therefore he multiplies his forgiveness.

**18:13** The compassion of a person is for his neighbor, but the compassion of the LORD is for all flesh; he rebukes, trains, teaches, and turns them back like a shepherd with his flock.

**18:14** He has compassion on those who accept correction and who eagerly seek his decrees.

**18:15** My child, do not add reproach to your good deeds, or harsh words to any of your gifts.

**18:16** Does not dew relieve the heat? So a word is worth more than a gift.

**18:17** Indeed, is not a good word worth more than a gift? Yet both are found in a gracious person.

**18:18** A fool is ungracious and insulting, and a gift from a grudging person makes the eyes sting.

**18:19** Before you speak, learn; and before you fall ill, care for your health.

**18:20** Before judgment comes, examine yourself; at the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness.

**18:21** Before falling ill, humble yourself; and when you have sinned, show your repentance.

**18:22** Let nothing prevent you from paying a vow in due time, and do not wait until death to discharge it.

**18:23** Before making a vow, have yourself ready; and do not be like one who tempts the LORD.

**18:24** Think of the wrath at the end of days, and the moment of punishment when he turns his face away.

**18:25** In a time of plenty, think of want; in the days of wealth, recall poverty and need.

**18:26** From morning to evening conditions change; and all things move swiftly before the LORD.

**18:27** A wise person is careful in all things; and in days of sinfulness he guards against wrongdoing.

**18:28** Every intelligent person recognizes wisdom, and gives honor to the one who discovered her.

**18:29** Those who understand sayings have also become wise, and have poured out fitting proverbs.

**18:30** Do not follow your base desires, but restrain your appetites.

**18:31** If you gratify every longing of your soul, it will make you a laughingstock to your enemies.

**18:32** Do not revel in luxury, lest you be ruined by its cost.

**18:33** Do not make yourself a pauper by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
